title: Multilevel mechanistic phenotyping in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction – a prospective, longitudinal cohort study within the CRC 1470
summary:
The study investigates patients with clinically suspected heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), aiming to improve the characterisation of different disease stages and underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Based on established diagnostic criteria, participants are assigned to either an HFpEF cohort or a symptomatic comparison cohort. Comprehensive clinical and cardiovascular phenotyping enables the identification of early disease-related alterations and provides further insights into the development and progression of HFpEF.

In HFpEF, the heart muscle becomes stiff and cannot relax normally. Although the heart’s pumping strength may appear normal, it cannot fill with enough blood, and standard tests may not easily show this problem. Each participant will receive a thorough health assessment, including tests of the heart, blood vessels, lungs, kidney function, physical fitness, metabolism, and inflammation. We will also collect and store blood and other samples in a central biobank so all CRC research teams can use them to study HFpEF. Z02 also follows people who show early signs of heart problems or have conditions such as diabetes, obesity, or high blood pressure. By monitoring their health over time, we aim to understand how HFpEF develops, how it progresses, and how it might be detected or treated earlier.

interventions.name: The clinical core of CRC 1470 is a prospective single-centre cohort study of ambulatory patients of both sexes with diverse cardiovascular comorbidities (N=400). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Age ≥ 18 years 
2) Written informed consent
3.) The principal eligibility criteria include clinical manifestations of heart failure corresponding to NYHA functional class II or higher, a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of at least 50%, and increased circulating natriuretic peptide concentrations. In patients with sinus rhythm, NT-proBNP levels must exceed 125 pg/mL or BNP levels 35 pg/mL, whereas higher thresholds apply to patients with atrial fibrillation (NT-proBNP >365 pg/mL or BNP >105 pg/mL). Additionally, evidence of structural or functional cardiac alterations indicative of diastolic dysfunction is required.
4. The comparison group comprises two distinct groups: symptomatic participants (NYHA class ≥II) who do not fulfil the diagnostic criteria for HFpEF because NT-proBNP levels and/or echocardiographic structural or functional parameters do not meet the guideline-recommended diagnostic thresholds, and asymptomatic participants (NYHA class I) with cardiovascular risk factors, classified according to the AHA/ACC heart failure Stage A–B. These participants are intentionally retained as an age- and symptom-matched comparison group, enabling separate characterisation of disease-progression gradations across the HFpEF spectrum.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Life expectancy < 1 year
2) Lack of consent or ability to give consent.
3) History of heart failure with reduced systolic function (HFmrEF u. HFrEF, LVEF< 50%); exception: acute heart failure, e.g. acute drop in LVEF during episodes of paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation with evidence of preserved LVEF in sinus rhythm
4) Terminal renal failure and/or need for dialysis.
5)
Myocardial infarction (ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction or non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction), urgent or elective percutaneous coronary intervention within the past 30 days
6) Cardiac surgery or other major cardiovascular surgery within the past three months
7) Alternative cardiac diagnoses that the investigator believes may be causing the patient's heart failure symptoms (evidence of severe right heart failure in the absence of left ventricular structural changes, specific etiologies such as infiltrative, genetically hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, constrictive pericarditis, sarcoidosis, amyloidosis, other storage diseases, clinically significant congenital heart disease, high-grade valvular vitiation requiring surgical or interventional management).
8) Alternative non-cardiac diagnoses that the investigator believes may be causing the patient's heart failure symptoms such as severe pulmonary disease (e.g., primary pulmonary hypertension, severe COPS GOLD >2) or severe anemia (Hb<10g/dl in men and Hb <9.5g/dl in women).
